title: Al Barsha 3 area guide
excerpt: Everything you need to know about living, buying and renting in Al Barsha 3.
intro: Al Barsha 3 is a residential community offering a quieter Dubai lifestyle with convenient access to major roads, schools, retail and everyday amenities.
about: The area offers a mix of villas and family-oriented residential surroundings. Its location makes it practical for residents who want access to central Dubai while maintaining a more spacious neighbourhood environment.
living: Residents benefit from nearby retail, dining, parks and family facilities. The wider Al Barsha district also provides easy access to major destinations across Dubai.
market: Property values and rental demand can vary significantly depending on property type, condition, size and exact location within the community.
schools: Families have access to a range of schools and educational facilities across the wider Al Barsha area.
lifestyle: The area is suited to residents looking for a community-oriented lifestyle with convenient access to retail, leisure and green spaces.
transport: Road connectivity makes the community practical for residents travelling across Dubai.

title: Arjan area guide
excerpt: A fast-growing residential district combining attainable apartment living, strong rental demand and convenient access to key Dubai corridors.
intro: Arjan has evolved from an emerging Dubailand address into a more established mid-market residential community. Its appeal comes from a practical mix: modern apartment stock, everyday services, proximity to Dubai Science Park and major road connections, plus a growing pipeline of new projects. In 2026, average sale prices sit around AED 1,575 per sq. ft. (up 8.42% year on year), average rent runs approximately AED 109 per sq. ft., and Bayut's H1 2026 report puts indicative apartment ROI at around 7.10%.
about: Arjan sits within Dubailand, close to Al Barsha South and Dubai Science Park. The community was launched as part of the wider Dubailand master plan and is now characterised by low- to mid-rise apartment buildings, newer residential developments, supermarkets, cafés, gyms, clinics and family-oriented services. For residents, Arjan offers a quieter alternative to denser central districts while remaining connected to major employment and lifestyle hubs by road. For investors, it is increasingly viewed as a yield-focused apartment market with a comparatively accessible entry point and a deep pipeline of off-plan supply.
living: Arjan's lifestyle is practical rather than ultra-urban. Residents have supermarkets, cafés, pharmacies, fitness facilities and neighbourhood retail within the district, while larger malls and entertainment destinations are a short drive away. Dubai Miracle Garden and the neighbouring Dubai Butterfly Garden are the community's best-known landmarks, and many newer buildings incorporate pools, gyms, landscaped areas, children's play zones, roof decks and wellness facilities, making the building itself an important part of the lifestyle proposition.
market: Arjan's property market continued to appreciate through 2026. Bayut's June 2026 index placed the community-wide average sale price at approximately AED 1,575 per sq. ft., up 8.42% year on year — studios lead at around AED 1,719 per sq. ft. (+6.99%), with three-bedrooms showing the strongest annual growth at +10.90%. Off-plan property in Arjan averaged around AED 1,606 per sq. ft., roughly 9.66% higher than a year earlier, reflecting the newer specification of current launches. On the rental side, Bayut's June 2026 index showed an average of approximately AED 109 per sq. ft., around 2.35% higher than 12 months earlier, though studios and one-bedrooms posted positive annual growth while larger units were flatter or softer over the same period. H1 2026 data puts the average transaction price at approximately AED 970,764 with an indicative apartment ROI of around 7.10% — an area-level indication rather than a guaranteed return for any individual unit.
schools: Arjan benefits from its position beside established family communities. A range of schools and nurseries can be found in Arjan, Al Barsha South, Motor City and nearby districts, including Safa Community School, Brighton College Dubai, Nord Anglia International School Dubai and Dubai Heights Academy. Healthcare access is also one of the community's practical strengths — clinics operate within Arjan, while Mediclinic Parkview Hospital is located nearby, giving residents access to a full-service hospital without travelling to central Dubai. School fees, curricula, admission availability and healthcare services change over time, so families should verify current details directly with each institution before making a relocation decision.
lifestyle: Arjan is well suited to young professionals working in Dubai Science Park, Barsha, Dubai Hills or western Dubai; couples and small families wanting modern apartments and nearby schools without moving into a premium central district; first-time buyers prioritising a more manageable total purchase price; and yield-focused or off-plan investors comparing mid-market apartment communities for rental returns. The community remains an active off-plan market through 2026-2029, with new launches increasingly competing on private pools, wellness spaces, co-working areas, smart-home systems and flexible payment plans. Buyers considering off-plan should compare developer track record, price per sq. ft. against ready resale alternatives, payment plan versus total purchase price, expected service charges, handover timeline and likely tenant profile at completion before committing.
transport: Arjan is positioned near Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road (E311) and Umm Suqeim Road (D63), giving drivers direct access toward Al Barsha, Dubai Hills, Motor City, JVC, Dubai Marina and central Dubai — one of the area's strongest practical advantages. Mall of the Emirates, reachable via Umm Suqeim Road, is also the nearest major Red Line Metro connection for onward travel. Public transport is improving but Arjan remains more convenient for residents who drive or use taxis and ride-hailing, since the community does not currently have its own Metro station — worth factoring in for tenants who rely heavily on rail transport.
